diagnosis.failure_category_label: Tool error — linter missing a rule; production code is correct

root_cause.summary: lint_sql_param_types.py only checks two C42883 patterns. It has no rule for 42P18.
detail: ASYMMETRIC_TEXT_CAST_RE detects: col::text = $N where $N lacks ::type (C42883 asymmetric cast on named UUID/bigint columns).
TEXT_COLUMNS_VS_INT_RE detects: WHERE version = <integer_literal> (integer literal compared to TEXT column).
No rule exists for: bare $N inside jsonb_build_object(...) or json_build_object(...) variadic-any function calls (42P18 untyped parameter).
PostgreSQL cannot infer parameter type for variadic-any functions at PREPARE time, raising ERROR 42P18: could not determine data type of parameter $N.
The ISS-0120 regression (WF03-GH383) was exactly this: jsonb_build_object('restored_orphan_reason', $2) with no ::text cast. The linter did not catch it.

evidence: tools/lint_sql_param_types.py: two regex rules only, both target C42883.
src/engine/reconstruction.zig:319 (fixed): was jsonb_build_object('restored_orphan_reason', $2) — bare, no cast. Now $2::text.
src/definition/promotion.zig:422 comment: 'This avoids the pg.zig parameter-type-inference failure that occurs when $N parameters appear inside jsonb_build_object() variadic arguments.'
Baseline scan (scratch/_iss0632_scan.py over src/ + tests/): zero existing bare $N in jsonb_build_object blocks — codebase is currently clean.
python3 tools/lint_sql_param_types.py src tests → Summary: 0 BLOCKER, 0 MAJOR, 0 MINOR (exit 0). Confirms new rule will NOT break the current clean state.

design_recommendation.approach: Add a new MAJOR rule using a paren-depth scan (not pure line-by-line regex) to find bare $N parameters inside jsonb_build_object / json_build_object blocks.
algorithm: 1. For each .zig file, read full text content.
a. Walk forward tracking paren depth to find the matching closing paren.
b. Extract the full block content (between the outer parens).
c. Within the block, find all $N occurrences using re.finditer(r'\$(\d+)(?!\s*::)', block).
d. For each match: compute line number from offset, emit a MAJOR finding.
3. Integrate into the existing lint_file() function or a new lint_file_variadic() helper called from lint_tree().
4. Severity: MAJOR (not BLOCKER) — same as TEXT_COLUMNS_VS_INT_RE, consistent with the ISS-0632 candidate_resolution.
design_recommendation.message_template: bare parameter $N inside {func}() variadic-any call — PostgreSQL cannot infer type at PREPARE time (42P18). Add $N::type cast (e.g. $N::text, $N::uuid, $N::bigint). See ISS-0632.

false_positive_analysis.set_config: set_config('key', $1, false) — NOT variadic-any; PostgreSQL infers types from fixed signature. NOT flagged (function name not in scope list).
false_positive_analysis.insert_values: INSERT INTO t (...) VALUES ('literal', $N, ...) — NOT inside jsonb_build_object; NOT flagged by paren-depth scan.
false_positive_analysis.already_cast_params: jsonb_build_object('k', $N::text) — $N::text has :: so regex (?!\s*::) does not match. NOT flagged.
false_positive_analysis.expression_values: jsonb_build_object('k', gen_random_uuid()::text) — no $N pattern. NOT flagged.
false_positive_analysis.confirmed_zero_fp: Baseline scan over current src/ + tests/ produced zero findings, confirming no false positives on clean code.

scope_notes: json_build_object() has the same variadic-any signature as jsonb_build_object — include both.

ARRAY[$N] constructor — PostgreSQL CAN infer element type from ARRAY context if all elements are the same type; leave out of scope.
